name: Tholpetty (Tholpetty range, Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary)
tagline: Northern Wayanad's quiet safari range — better visibility after the monsoon
summary: Tholpetty is the northern safari range of Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary. After the monsoon the forest dries, animals concentrate near water and visibility improves for jeep safaris and birding.
description: Tholpetty is the northern range and visitor gate of the Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary (part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve), reached from the Mananthavady–Kutta road. The range borders Nagarhole (Karnataka) and covers moist deciduous and semi‑evergreen forest.

Forest Department–operated jeep safaris run from the Tholpetty checkpost in morning and afternoon slots; tickets and a departmental guide are compulsory. The range is quieter than Muthanga and is prized for elephants, gaur, deer, Malabar giant squirrel, occasional big cats and rich birdlife.

Seasonality strongly affects sightings: immediately after the monsoon the forest is lush but visibility is low; as the dry season progresses (roughly October–May, with peak visibility December–April) water becomes scarce, animals concentrate around remaining waterholes and visibility in the understorey improves — making post‑monsoon safaris especially productive for wildlife and birding.

Practical for day visitors based at Mananthavady or nearby homestays, Tholpetty pairs well with Thirunelli temple, Brahmagiri treks and northern Wayanad birding circuits. Confirm rules, timings and booking before you travel.
highlights: Northern range of Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary — quieter, less crowded than Muthanga
Forest Department jeep safaris (morning and afternoon slots)
Good for elephants, gaur, deer, Malabar giant squirrel and over 200–300 bird species
Post‑monsoon dry season improves visibility as animals gather at waterholes
Easy add‑on to Thirunelli temple and Brahmagiri area itineraries
Strict rules: compulsory guide/jeep, camera fees/camera rules and no private vehicles into core zones (confirm locally)

sections.heading: Background
body: Tholpetty is the northern visitor range of the Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary (not a separate park) and forms part of the larger Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve. The forest here is a mix of moist deciduous and semi‑evergreen types; the range shares ecological links with Karnataka’s Nagarhole and supports wide‑ranging species that move across state borders.

Ecotourism at Tholpetty is managed by the Kerala Forest Department and local eco‑development committees; visits are allowed only through authorised safari vehicles with departmental guides to minimise disturbance.

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: Take a Forest Department jeep safari (usually 1.5–2 hours) in the morning or late afternoon — these slots are timed for animal activity. Tholpetty is especially rewarding for birdwatchers and for steady sightings of elephants, gaur and deer; big cats are present but sightings are rare.

Bring binoculars and a camera (check camera/video fee rules at the counter). Pair a Tholpetty safari with nearby cultural and nature stops such as Thirunelli temple and short treks in the Brahmagiri foothills for a full northern Wayanad day.

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: Best window: October–May; peak dry‑season visibility and concentration of wildlife around water generally occurs December–April. Safaris may be limited or suspended during heavy monsoon months (June–September) and occasionally during fire‑risk periods — always confirm before you go.

Bookings: safaris are run by the Kerala Forest Department; some slots are available at the counter and some through official/forest ecotourism portals but booking systems and fee structures change — confirm the current procedure, fees and vehicle capacity before travel.

latest.text: A 2026 report of state permit portal changes noted that some Tholpetty online bookings were intermittently unavailable and that counter booking remained in use; fees and online availability can change seasonally.

Local reporting (June 11, 2026) noted the Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary reopening with revised/extended safari timings and an emphasis on online booking; Tholpetty is identified as one of the visitor ranges. Confirm current timings at the gate.

visitorInfo.bestTime: October–May; peak dry‑season visibility December–April (confirm for fire‑season closures).
visitorInfo.howToReach: Approach from Mananthavady (Tholpetty gate is roughly 20–24 km from Mananthavady on the Kodagu/ Kutta road). Nearest major airport is Calicut (Kozhikode) — confirm road times and local transport.
etiquette: Book or confirm safari slots and fees in advance where possible; the Forest Department issues permits and rules change seasonally.
Arrive before the counter opens for a better chance at an early morning slot; mornings and late afternoons are best for sightings.
Wear muted colours, stay silent in the jeep, and follow your guide’s instructions; private vehicles are not permitted inside core zones.
Carry water and light layers (early mornings are cool); check camera/video rules and avoid drones.
